contributions.statement: When an agent implements a spec decomposed into several units, keep each completed unit's acceptance tests as harness-owned regression obligations re-run at every checkpoint; agents author far fewer tests than the native suite and later edits regress earlier units that end-state scoring would miss.
contributions.evidence: §3.2 Table 3: authored test count (#T) markedly below native suite for every loop, Reg>0 in every profile; Table 4 regressions/run 0.13-0.36 even for the best loops. Tests largely LLM-synthesized, single trial per pairing.

contributions.statement: Do not rely on the agent to infer prerequisite order across a multi-unit task; recorded plans recovered only part of the source dependency DAG, and linear open-source harnesses planned near-chains.
contributions.evidence: §3.2 Table 3 Edge F1 and layer rho per harness; reference DAG is a lower bound (Limitations). Giving the DAG explicitly was not tested.

reason: Beyond the leaderboard, it measures that long-horizon agents under-test and regress earlier units, which backs harness-owned per-unit regression obligations in a spec rollout; the fixed-model harness comparison is undermined by a likely duplicated table row.
